“A Golden Gift to the White House for its 250th Birthday Year.”

For generations in America, eagle plaques were sometimes placed above homes once the mortgage had been paid off, a quiet declaration that the debt was settled, that the bank no longer owned the roof over your head, that the home truly belonged to the family that lived within it.

Since 1871 America has existed less as a fully sovereign republic and more as a debtor state, tied to a system of international finance that ultimately traces back through central banks, the City of London and the institutions of the old imperial order.

The golden eagle placed upon the White House might carry a very particular symbolism; the mortgage has been paid, the debt is settled. The house belongs to its rightful owners once again - we the people.
